Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 48 hr. Stepped Pressure Build-Up Tests (SPBUT) being performed on both wells on the DeWolf pad, the Evelyn Wyo. 4H and the Evelyn Wyo. 2H. These SPBUT's are being performed to access recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool) deployment that was performed on both wells on 12/20/20. (See attachments for each wells details. All shut-in pressures were monitored and recorded throughout testing period by CALLCs SCADA system. The Evelyn Wyo. 4H wells Conductor x Surface (20 x 13 3/8) annulus has an open casing top in cellar, the Evelyn Wyo. 2H Conductor by Surface (20 x13 3/8) annulus is capped and set up for venting to atmosphere via a 1" pipe to surface and a Sentry valve. For the (PBUTs), this annulus was shut in on 2/2/21 @ ~ 07:30. All well cellars were filled with water and frozen w/ no active bubbling noted in cellars at time of inspection. Both wells remained in production through the SPBUT period. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Denny DeWolf and Creston Consultant Reps. Shane Reimold and Alex Pashchuk. Gas detections were then confirmed by The Department, using a MSA ALTAIR 5X gas meter, last calibrated on 1/11/21. Creston Consultant collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/16/2025 to EQT PROD CO in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland county. 91.33(B)_ - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to remove from the ground and from the affected waters of this Commonwealth the residual substances contained thereon or therein within 15 days from a pollution or a danger of pollution incident.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT PROD CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/16/2025
Violation Code: 91.33(B)_ - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to remove from the ground and from the affected waters of this Commonwealth the residual substances contained thereon or therein within 15 days from a pollution or a danger of pollution incident.
Violation ID: 8241768
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/16/2025
Comments: On July 16, 2025 DEP conducted an Incident Inspection of EQT's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County. EQT acquired the Porter Well Pad from Olympus on 7/1/2025 (Transfer approved by the DEP on 7/14/2025), therefore EQT takes full responsibility of the incident addressed in IR 4004278, where violations were issued for a 1-3 barrel release of a produced water, freshwater and frack chemical mixture. Accompanying during today's inspection was EQT's Lance Barnes, Olympus's Kyle Borden and SPSI's Joe Perry.At the time of this inspection an Act 9 sign was observed at the access road entrance and in the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan. Operator information on the sign does not match the plans. The DEP recommends the Operator promptly update the plans as applicable. An access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed.During IR 4004278, the DEP screened the release area and collected elevated conductivity readings in an area that was scraped 2-4 inches deep as well as at the base/underneath an AST (inadvertently referred to as freshwater impoundment in IR 4004278) on site. At the time of that inspection, Olympus's Laura Karosic stated once fracking is complete (7/11-12/ 2024), the AST would be removed from the well site and further remediation efforts would be conducted in the release area.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the AST to be removed from the well site. The area where the AST was as well as the previously scraped release area all appeared to be newly scraped. A ditch was observed to be dug and bordering the secondary containment within the release area. The DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the newly scraped release area as well as the ditch. The DEP collected soil readings of 0.0171 mS, 0.0605 mS, and 0.026 mS in the newly scraped release area, and 2.33 mS in a puddle of cloudy fluid observed in the ditch. These conductivity readings were compared to a background soil reading taken on the well site perimeter (0.1247 mS). The readings collected in the scraped areas are comparable to the background reading, however readings collected in the ditch are elevated. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Barnes and Mr. Perry informed the DEP that the observed to be newly scraped release area is reportedly remediated, however the ditch and area underneath the containment is not. The DEP inquired why/how the area under the containment is contaminated when the release originated on top of the containment. Mr. Perry hypothesized that released fluids that were sitting on the graveled well pad/under the AST were washed underneath the secondary containment during heavy rainfall following the release. Once the rain ceased and the AST was removed, contaminated fluids leached out from under the containment in the release area, therefore the ditch is being utilized to catch and contain any of the leached contaminated fluid. Mr. Barnes and Mr. Borden stated that drilling will be completed in approx. 8-10 days, then the containment will be pulled and remediation efforts will be conducted in the remaining contaminated locations.The DEP recommends the EQT promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).During IR 4004278 the DEP requested the following:-The Operator submit a written response that includes an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released.-The Operator follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) -The Operator assess the impacts to the WOC from the release.-The Operator submit a NOV response by 7/23/25.--These have yet to be received as of 7/16/25Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued to EQT for the 1-3 barrel release and for failure to remove the contaminated fluid from the ground within 15 days of the pollution incident.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8166299
Permit API: 081-20763
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lewis Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/27/2023
Comments: On November 27, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the Range Resources Cornwall Mountain 1-8H. This is to follow up with a reported spill by Range Resources on the afternoon of November 25, 2023 of approximately a barrel of production fluid. The production fluid was noticed bubbling from the well pad surface in the area of the buried dump line for the GPUs. The buried dump line from GPU 4 was immediately isolated. Range Resources found a small hole in the the buried dump line from the GPU to the production fluid tanks during the initial excavation where the bubbling was occurring. Upon arrival, Range Resources had dug three pilot holes along the dump line to aid in delineating the extent of the impact from the hole in the line. Three more pilot holes were dug during the inspection moving toward the production fluid tanks. The pilot holes were dug by a mobile high vacuum system. The last pilot hole dug, closest to the production fluid tanks, had a soil conductivity of less than 1,000 uS/cm. Range Resources conducted screening of the soil conductivity of the pilot holes and the conductivity ranged from less than 1,000 uS/cm to 4,650 uS/cm. Range Resources said that the production fluid that spilled seemed to follow the path of the dump line from the GPUs and did not appear to leave the well pad. DEP did not observe any seeps or erosion off the well pad edge indicating the production fluid had left the well pad. Kirby Steck with Range Resources said with digging the pilot holes they now know the extent of the area they need to excavate along the dump line. Range Resources plans to begin excavating the area around the GPU dump line to remove the impacted soil. The impacted soil will be placed in a roll off dumpster which was in containment. Once the area has been excavated, Range Resources plans on contacting Moody and Associates to collect the Act 2 confirmatory soil samples. The spilling of production fluid outside of containment onto the well pad surface cause violations of the Clean Stream Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301.

Report Details
Operator: Cnx Gas Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-02-04
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 841800
Permit API: 125-23238
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Morris Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-02-04
Comments: On Friday February 1, 2019 I received notification of a produced water release at the NV72 CBM Well Site located in Morris Township, Washington County. On the same day, I spoke on the telephone with Mr. Kyle Borden from CNX Resources Partners (CNX) regarding details of the release and remediation efforts. On Monday February 4, 2019 I conducted a site inspection to further assess the situation. Following the inspection, I was contacted via telephone by Mr. Borden with an update to CNX's continued investigation which was completed prior to my inspection. There are five (5) production tanks connected in succession within a vegetated earthen berm containment structure which receives produced water from multiple gas wells in the area. The produced water enters tank 1 and will flow into each successive tank dependent upon the fluid level in the preceding tank. The fluid within the hose connecting tank 1 and tank 2 had become frozen during the recent polar vortex which impeded movement of fluid between the two tanks, thereby causing fluid from tank 1 to flow out of the top of the tank and into the containment structure. CNX estimated that approximately one (1) barrel of produced water flowed from the tank and into the berm structure which had ice coating the floor of the structure. The produced water had settled in a low spot within the berm structure near tank 1. The pooled water within the berm was vacuumed out of the berm with a vacuum truck. CNX arranged to have a vacuum truck return to the site to continue removing fluid from within the berm as the temperature continued to rise over the weekend and the ice within the berm melted. Representatives of CNX returned to the site on Monday morning, February 4, 2019, to continue their investigation and delineate any potential impact. Soil conductivity probe readings, ranging from less than one (1) mS/cm and not more than three (3) mS/cm were collected within the berm. Soil samples were collected from areas where the highest readings were observed for laboratory analysis to further determine impact. CNX will send the analytical results and a written summary of investigation activities to the Department for review upon receipt. During my Monday afternoon site inspection, soil conductivity readings were collected with a portable probe in accessible areas around tank 1 and tank 2. A part of the area was still covered in ice, ranging between one (1) and three (3) inches thick. Sections of the ground, not covered with ice, were observed to be frozen given the probe temperature readings and difficulty penetrating the earth with the probe. Readings around tank 1 ranged from less than one (1) mS/cm to just over one (1) mS/cm. Readings collected from the berm in front of tank 1 were less than one (1) mS/cm. The common value of two (2) to three (3) mS/cm used to remediate soils impacted by brine was not exceeded by readings collected by CNX and the Department. The release of fluid from the production tank and into the earthen berm structure surrounding the production tanks is a violation of 25 Pa. Code Section 78.54, 25 Pa. Code Section 78.57(a) and 35 P.S. Section 6018.301 (SWMA 301). The operator should respond in accordance with instructions in this notice.

Comments: On 05/14/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the Cogar Well Site following an incident report received by the Department on 05/12/2025 (CTS 389093). SPSI crew on site remediating. The operator reported a spill to the Department on 05/13/2025 regarding more than 5 gallons of production water that were released on a load out pumpkin. No waterways were affected. The incident occurred on 05/12/2025 and reported over two hours after the incident on 05/13/2025. The following was observed:The area of impact was adjacent to the containment of the production tanks. SPSI excavated the impacted area to determine the extent of impact and place waste in roll off dumpsters. The area of impact was under the load out pumpkin and where the cement containment would be. A portion of the dump line was exposed during excavation. Water was pooling within the excavated area (Photos 1-6).Conductivity readings were taken within the area of impact. Readings were 5.23, 7.60, 13.62, 14.27, 16.22 mS/cm, and Over Range (Photos 7-14).Additional readings taken within the upper layers of substrate and clay layer were 430, 533, 850, and 968 uS/cm (Photos 15-18).The cement containment had a reading of Over Range. There appeared to be residual fluid combined with rainwater (Photo 19).The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan were on site (Photo 20).Due to the release of production fluid greater than 5 gallons and failure to report a reportable spill within 2 hours, violations of 78a54, SWMA 301, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), 78a66(b)2 are being issued. The Department requests an updated estimation of the quantity of production fluid released. The Department requests information on if the operator intends to remediate per Act 2 guidelines regarding the quantity released.

Temporary stabilization appears to be inadequate (Photo 13 & 14), the Department recommends that the operator reapply temp stabilization or take other remedial actions to temp stabilize the well pad.Based on this inspection, violations related to BMPs and stabilization will remain outstanding. No active discharges are observed, as such CSL 402(b) will be closed as corrected/abated. Pending further investigation and review and receipt of the operators response, more violations may be issued.

Violation ID: 8254155
Permit API: 115-23194
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/27/2025
Comments: On 10/27/25 I was at the Coterra Energy Lauer D. Well Site from 1327 to 1459 hours to perform a follow up inspection in response to the report a release of an unknown volume of natural gas and production fluid out of the Lauer D 12H well on 10/22/25. The weather conditions are mostly sunny skies with a light wind and temperatures in the low to mid 50's. The intent of the inspection is to evaluate the impact to the ground surface of the well pad from the release of production fluid. Shortly after arrival I met with Brendon Logan, Environmental Health and Safety Specialist. We walked to the location on the site where a sump (Sump # 1) was constructed on 10/22/25 in a drainage channel adjacent to and west of the access road near the well pad entrance. Sump # 1 is collecting fluid which released out of the 12H well onto the well pad and flowed into a drainage channel on the western side of the pad. Fluid in Sump # 1 is transferred via a pump into a frac tank in a containment structure. I utilized a Hanna HI 98331 Groline Soil Test Meter and an Oakton PCTS 5 meter to perform field screening of specific conductance (electrical conductivity, EC) in wet soil in the drainage channel adjacent to Sump #1 and in fluid pooled in this sump. Mr. Logan and I walked in a counter clockwise direction starting in the infiltration basin south of the well pad and in between the tank pad and well pad around the perimeter of the pad in the basin, to the northeast corner of the pad, then across the north side of the pad, and then to the center of the pad near the wells. I also performed conductivity screening in wet soil and fluid in the infiltration basin south and east of the well pad inside of the LOD and on the pad surface near the wells and equipment designated for frac operations. Conductivity readings in fluid in Sump # 1 and in a sump constructed just east and adjacent to the access road and south of the well pad in an infiltration basin, (Sump#2), and on the well pad, are indicative of a spill of production fluid. I also met with Brody Webster, Andy Mehalko, and Mike Oakley of Coterra during the inspection. Coterra is in the process of preparing to remediate (clean up) impacted pad material in association with the release of production fluid. Coterra has removed a section of the secondary containment liner near the wells and rig mats in order to evaluate the extent of the impact and remove impacted material. Coterra informed me that they plan to remove additional equipment designated for frac operations and commence the remediation process via the use of heavy equipment tomorrow, 10/29/25. See photos for additional details. Please feel free to contact me @ 570-346-5533 or jsassi@pa.gov should you have any questions.

Report Details

Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Greene Twp

Inspection Date: 2020-02-18
Comments: On 02/14/2020 WQS Kristof Eichenlaub conducted incident response inspection # 2999089 On 02/18/2020 at approximately 1350 I conducted a follow up inspection at the site. Foamer product and sediment laden water were discharging from the sediment basin outlet, overwhelming two silt socks, and discharging outside the LOD into UNT 8 to Frosty Run. The discharge caused accelerated erosion below the silt socks and extending into UNT 8 to Frosty Run. A contractor for Greylock was utilizing a bucket and a pressurized sprayer bottle in an attempt to remove foamer product from the sediment basin rip rap outlet. I inquired what the contractor was utilizing to eliminate the foam. The contractor informed me they were utilizing fabric softener. I contacted Greylock Regulatory Compliance Coordinator Keith Eighmey via phone, who indicated he was unaware of the contractor's activities. Eighmey indicated Greylock had previously utilized a defoaming agent in the channels and basin to eliminate foamer product. Eighmey indicated Greylock could provide the SDS for the defoaming agent. The Department requests Greylock provide the SDS for the defoaming agent. The spill had not been remediated and was continuing to discharge to UNT 8 to Frosty Run. A sediment laden water discharge to UNT 8 to Frosty Run was also continuing. Greylock discharged an additional substance to Waters of the Commonwealth during their attempt to remove the foamer. Some violations are ongoing as a result of a spill that was documented on 02/14/2020 (inspection # 2999089). Additional violations of CSL 301 and 307 have occurred due to Greylock discharging a chemical to UNT 8 to reduce the surfactant foam. A violation of OGA3259(2I) has occurred for failure to comply with DEP cleanup order issued on 02/14/2020.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of at least 5 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and stormwater was discovered on the well pad following a re-frac on the 5H well. The notification also stated that a contractor, Tobias, would excavate the impacted pad material. I met with company man Levi Lee upon arriving on location. He showed me the location of the release. Violation ID: 995303
Permit API: 015-21185
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/08/2023
Comments: On 5/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident inspection at the Repsol Alderson V 05-009 well site. This was in response to a spill notification of five gallons of antifreeze that the department received from Repsol on 5/6/2023.Prior to arrival at the site, I contacted JD Ressler of Repsol, the person who had submitted the notification of the spill to the department. JD said that at approximately 2:30 AM on 5/6/2023, a truck driver drove over a concrete barricade, dragging the barricade along under his truck for a distance on the pad surface. The concrete barricade did damage an antifreeze line on the truck, releasing approximately 5 gallons of antifreeze to the pad surface. Upon discovery, the leak was stopped and oil soaks were placed on the pad surface to absorb the fluid. The contaminated oil soaks were placed into trash bags. This waste material was brought to the Warner 05121 well site in Susquehanna county where fracking operations are currently being conducted. The waste material will be disposed by Environmental Resources out of Tunkhannock, PA.It was 55 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. Repsol is using the Alderson V 009 location to stage trucks that are servicing a nearby frac site in Susquehanna County. Sand and water trucks were on location, driving in and out during the inspection. At the site, I met with Repsol's Andrew Senefelder. Andrew led me to the location of the spill. Andrew said that the truck driver did run over and drag one concrete block, and also drug another concrete block that was attached via a cable. These concrete blocks are approximately 2' x 2' x 8' and can be viewed in pictures 3 and 4. I did look around the area described as where the spill took place. I screened water puddles in the area for conductivity with results at 0.4 mS conductance or less. I also viewed the puddles and the surface of the ground. I did not witness any discoloration or evidence of contamination in this area. Discussing the location of the waste, Andrew did say that the contaminated material was being brought back to this well site and would be disposed of from this site.Water puddles from recent rainfall were scattered across the pad surface. I field tested these for conductivity with results at 0.4 mS or less. I did not witness the emergency response plan at the entrance to the facility. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by two bio retention basins. Bio retention basin 1 is adequately stabilized and functioning as designed with minimal evidence of standing water. Bio retention basin 2 does have wetland foliage and standing water.There was one well staged for production. The well was tagged with the API/well permit number. No bubbling within the cellar was observed. The GPU and production tank had secondary containment. This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; SWMA 301, CSL 402, and 25 PA Code 78a.56. The spill had been cleaned up, resulting in VIOICs (Violation noted and Immediately Corrected).The DEP recommends the following: 1. Screen the area impacted by the release of antifreeze for additional contamination and continue with cleanup as necessary.2. Assess the stability and functionality of bio retention basin 2 and repair as necessary.3. Place a copy of the site emergency response plan at the entrance to the facility.I left the site at 1330 hours.

Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/05/2025
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 8232014
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/05/2025
Comments: Site inspection conducted to review drill cuttings processing activity and secondary containment conditions at the Taft 851 well pad. Meeting on site today with Seneca Company Man Carlos Martinez. Weather conditions are foggy with light rain and 60F.According to Mr. Martinez, the Patterson 805 rig is drilling the 12 1/4 intermediate section on the 206HU well (API # 117- 22267). This is the first of eight total to be drilled. The intermediate casing is expected to be cemented on Wednesday evening at a depth of 3,329'. The 206HU will be drilled top to total depth with the rig batch drilling the surface and intermediate sections for the remaining seven wells. There are five wells in production and currently flowing to sales at this pad. Fluid control in the rig backyard is being handled by Paragon Integrated Services. The rig is drilling the intermediate string on water based mud (WBM) with polymer flocculants and calcium nitrate in use to assist removal of solids from the drilling fluid. Drill cuttings are removed from the system using two sets of shakers and two centrifuges. Fluid removed from the centrifuges is returned to a catch tank and pumped back to the mud tanks for recirculation downhole (photos 3-5). Solids control in the backyard is being conducted by White's Energy Services. Drill cuttings and excess liquid are solidified using wood crumble material and are stored in steel bins awaiting haulage to the landfill. Seneca submitted a Request for Approval of Alternate Waste Management Practices (OG-71) Form A application for the Taft Pad on 4/25/25. The Department approved the request on 5/1/25. The request for the approval of Alternative Waste Management Practices is for drill cuttings processing and solids removal from drilling mud. See photos and comments in the on-site processing findings section of this inspection report below, and refer to the Taft OG-71 Form A application, eFACTS Authorization ID#1525611.Site inspection followed several days of heavy precipitation. A vacuum truck is pumping precipitation water out of secondary containment structures for the frac tank battery at the west side of the pad. The Department observed yellow floc water tanks labeled as cement water near the north side of the rig. The Department recommends that floc water tanks and freshwater tanks near the barite silos be labeled for contents. During this inspection, fluid with elevated conductivity (4.74 mS/cm) is observed in the ditch line between the pad rock and the berm along the north side of the well pad (photo 13). This water was traced and found to be entering Sediment Basin 1 along the rock lined channel sloping down from the pad surface. Additionally, water was observed draining from the sed basin, entering the level spreader, and exiting to a brushy wooded area north of the LOD with a conductivity reading of 2.16 mS/cm. The Department recommends containing and collecting water which exceeds the Department 78a.60b(3) discharge limitation of 1,000 uS/cm or 1 mS/cm. Violations remain outstanding against permit #117-22231 for pollutional water found on site and documented in Inspection Reports #3736567 and #3724668.
